text:
incident-bot: ALERT: P99 latency spike detected for dedicated-pool eu-west-1 (p99 ~= 6.2s, p95 ~= 1.9s) — auto-page to #incidents (svc: redwood-runtime, route: /v1/generate)

maria-ops: oncall here, landing. seeing a big tail in streaming. p99 jumped at 09:14 UTC, roughly when a burst came in from a high-throughput tenant.

ryan-sre: joining. AWS autoscaler logs show ASG scaling events delayed ~70-95s for new warmup slots. handshake timeouts visible in svc logs.

alex-ml: reproducing: streaming stalls where the tail RPCs hang for ~4–6s, not continuous token generation. KV cache coldpath spiky. suspicion: cold pools + autoscale handshake delay.

john-support: Customer impact: 2 enterprise customers (cust-prod-a, cust-recommender) reported errors and UI stalls ~09:15–09:24 UTC. CS already informed them we're investigating.

olivia-eng: metrics snapshot:
- queue_depth (dedicated-eu-west-1): 4620 -> peaked 5k
- nodes_active: 18 -> should be 32 under policy
- warmup_rate: ~0.6 nodes/min (should be ~2.5)
- streaming_stalls: +420% last 10m

maria-ops: important: streaming stalls correlate with queue depth spikes. lower-priority hotshot requests are saturating handshake slots. We'll throttle priority less-critical routes.

ryan-sre: checked autoscaler: controller tried to request more capacity but cloud provider queued the requests; cloud returns instances but our warmup/handshake agent takes ~90s to register on routing. BAU is ~20–30s. Need immediate mitigation.

alex-ml: put a quick check in logs: handshake failures show TL;DR: grpc dial timeouts to runtime-hotshot-init (logs attached).

olivia-eng: Proposed live mitigations: 1) temporarily shift routing policy to prefer prewarmed dedicated backup pool eu-west-2; 2) enable conservative dequeue to avoid head-of-line blocking for streaming; 3) bump priority for enterprise customers.

maria-ops: I'm doing 1) now — routing override to eu-west-2 for flagged customers (cust-prod-a, cust-recommender). Will monitor impact.

oncall-bot: action: routing override applied by maria-ops at 09:22 UTC (route: /v1/generate -> eu-west-2 fallback).

john-support: support note: informing cust-prod-a that we routed traffic to fallback region; might see slight latency increase but stable responses.

ryan-sre: 2) implemented conservative dequeue: set consumer.max_in_flight=8 to reduce multiplexing pressure (temporary). Observed immediate p99 drop to ~3.2s on a subset.

alex-ml: also purged KV cache cold-writes backlog on a few nodes (manual kick) — this reduces cold path stalls.

olivia-eng: telemetry: after routing override + dequeue change:
- queue_depth down to ~900 in eu-west-1
- p99 global ~2.8s, p95 ~1.2s
- streaming_stalls down ~60%

maria-ops: good progress. however autoscaler still showing slow handshake; need root cause: either kernel/network or warmup init sequence throttling. Ryan, can you escalate to infra if we see more >75s handshakes?

ryan-sre: yup I'll open infra-bridge and escalate to cloud provisioning. Also collecting tcpdump on init path.

alex-ml: hypothesis: when cold pools spin up, model weights load/unpack + quantization kernel init cause long process startup; combined with grpc backoff, we get long register time. We should consider async warmup or prefetching keys for these customers.

john-support: CH status update: cust-prod-a acknowledges mitigation; they still reported a couple stalled sessions but no errors now. Cust-recommender seeing improvements too.

maria-ops: can someone confirm if dedicated hotshot pool quota was exhausted? Logs show 0 spare hotshot slots at peak.

olivia-eng: pool util at peak: 100% hotshot usage and 12 pending warmups. autoscaler min reserve was 0. We should discuss increasing reserve or prewarmed buffer for business critical tiers.

ryan-sre: infra responded: cloud provider had transient API throttling backing scale requests — extended warmup delay. Raised priority with provider support.

alex-ml: quick patch deployed (hotfix): reduce model weight unpack IO priority & parallelize per-GPU init to shorten warmup by ~30%. Rolling to 5% -> 50% -> 100%.

maria-ops: rolling looks good, metrics improving. p99 sliding toward 1.6s. Keeping routing override for another 15m.

oncall-bot: incident severity lowered to SEV2 at 09:38 UTC — customer-impact reduced (still ongoing mitigation).

john-support: customers updated: cust-prod-a & cust-recommender notified of mitigation and ETA for full restoration: 30m. They requested postmortem.

olivia-eng: quick post-incident notes for PM/ops: root causes suspected
- autoscaler-cloud API throttling causing instance provisioning delays
- insufficient prewarmed buffer for dedicated hotshot pool for enterprise tier
- model warmup sequence (IO + kernel init) prolonging handshake registration

maria-ops: immediate action items (short):
- Increase reserved prewarmed capacity for enterprise customers (deploy config change) — owner: olivia-eng — ETA 2h
- Add autoscaler retry/backoff guard and alert on handshake >45s — owner: ryan-sre — ETA 4h
- Improve warmup init parallelism & IO prioritization (ship follow-up patch) — owner: alex-ml — ETA 24h
- Update runbook for routing fallback steps + customer comms template — owner: john-support — ETA 6h

ryan-sre: long-term: evaluate async model weight prefetch and maintain a small hot reserve per region. Also add synthetic tail tests to catch handshake regressions.

maria-ops: handing off to ryan-sre for overnight followup. I'm off-call in 20m. Thanks team.

ryan-sre: taking over oncall. I'll keep this thread updated with RCA progress and the infra provider ticket #CLOUD-7891.

olivia-eng: noted. will schedule postmortem doc and link to this thread.

john-support: will draft customer-facing timeline + root-cause summary after RCA.

maria-ops: closing live mitigation window. leaving routing override in place until warmups stable. great job everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: NOTE: related metrics and logs archived to incident-runbook/1812504321 for postmortem.

ryan-sre: final: monitoring 30m; will clear routing override once warmup heat is healthy and p99 < 1.5s for 20m.

olivia-eng: postmortem link placeholder: /docs/postmortems/incident-1812504321 — will populate with timeline and traces.

john-support: ACK.

maria-ops: thanks — handing off complete. :wave:
